language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hello, my name is Oleif. Welcome to my ship!

Are you here to help? I sure could use an extra set of hands. There are plenty of chores on my ship! Today, I’m learning about matter. My ship is a magical ship – but only this thing called “matter” can make it move! I need to keep my boat moving! Can you help me?
But first things first: let’s find out what “matter” is and what it means to us.
Did you know that there are three types of matter?
There is solid matter like my shield or the ship’s sail.
There is liquid matter, like water.
And there is gas matter, like air or smoke.
I need all of them to make my ship sail, but I can’t have water on the deck or the sail in the water. So I need your help to distinguish the types for me. Would you do that for me? Great, thanks!
Oh, I almost forgot. There is one more thing you need to know about the three types of matter.
You see, all three of them are made up of something called “particles”. Particles are very small: so small you cannot even see them. All matter is made from these particles.
When particles are close together and don’t move much, the matter is a solid. Solids hold their shape.
When particles have some space to move, and take on the shape of the container they are in, the matter is liquid.
Matter with particles that move fast with lots of space between them are gases. Gases, like oxygen in the air we breathe, can be held in a container.
Help Oleif with his chores while he learns about matter!

Matter is anything that takes up space and has mass. My helmet, for instance, is a form of matter, because it both takes up space and has mass. My shadow is not a form of matter, because it has no mass.
Matter helps my ship move faster! Can you help me find matter?
